# Ascension perks

<div class="rr-stats"><div class="rr-stat"><span class="rr-stat-value">41</span><span class="rr-stat-label">perks on the wall</span></div><div class="rr-stat"><span class="rr-stat-value">5</span><span class="rr-stat-label">rarities</span></div><div class="rr-stat"><span class="rr-stat-value">35</span><span class="rr-stat-label">presses for a Legendary fill</span></div><div class="rr-stat"><span class="rr-stat-value">5</span><span class="rr-stat-label">start grant sockets at most</span></div></div>

After your first [ascension](basics.md#ascension), the **ASCENSION PERKS** card on UPGRADES opens a wall of perk cells you work with [Stardust](basics.md#stardust), the currency ascending pays.

Pick a rarity along the top, press a cell to pour Stardust into it, and the readout along the bottom shows what the perk does, what a press costs and how far the fill has got.

Every fill of every perk on the wall, leaving out the Limited perks, comes to **97,500 Stardust**, which is what the Wall of Fame [badge](badges.md) asks for. A Limited perk's cell stays locked until you clear its [challenge](challenges.md), and a Gold medal pours its first fill for free.

## Two fills a perk

Every perk is bought in two fills.

- The **first fill**, in the perk's own colour, is the first step toward the gold fill. Every perk can already turn up at gates without it. Common perks skip it.
- The **second fill**, in gold, makes it a **start grant**. Set it into a socket and every run starts with it, as if you had picked it at a gate.
- Stardust poured into a half full cell stays there, so you can stop and come back to it.
- The wall is locked while a run is live or [saved](basics.md#save-and-quit), because a new start grant would change that run.

## Layers and presses

A fill lays down layers of Stardust, one more for every step of rarity. The first layer takes **5 presses** and every layer above it takes 1 more. Hold a cell to keep pouring. A fill's price is split across its presses, so every press costs about the same.

| Rarity | Layers | Presses per layer | Presses a fill | First fill (Stardust) | Start grant (Stardust) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Common | 1 | 5 | 5 | Not needed | 900 |
| Uncommon | 2 | 5, 6 | 11 | 600 | 2,400 |
| Rare | 3 | 5, 6, 7 | 18 | 1,100 | 4,200 |
| Epic | 4 | 5, 6, 7, 8 | 26 | 2,100 | 7,200 |
| Legendary | 5 | 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 | 35 | 3,600 | 12,000 |

## Meeting a perk

Uncommon and rarer perks start out **not yet met**, and their cells stay locked until you have seen the perk at a biome gate. Seeing it is enough, even if you pick the other card. From then on you can work it on the wall. Its second fill, in gold, lets every run start with it and lets you bar it from gates.

## Start grant sockets

Your first ascension opens 1 start grant socket for free. The next 2 are bought with Stardust in order, 1,500 then 3,000, for 3 sockets. Press the next locked socket in the band at the top of the page to buy it. A bought socket is yours for good, and ascending never takes it back. The **Extra Sockets** pass in the [store](store.md) adds 2 more after those, for 5 in all. A start grant that needs something your run does not have yet, like a golden tile perk without Golden Tiles, is skipped that run.

| Socket | How it opens |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Free with your first ascension |
| 2 | 1,500 Stardust |
| 3 | 3,000 Stardust |
| 4 | The Extra Sockets pass |
| 5 | The Extra Sockets pass |

Sockets you can use always show first in the band, then the ones still to buy.

## Gate only

6 Common perks need something a bare run with no tree and no forge faces does not have, such as Golden Tiles, Gate Bonus, a Spark source or a Multi Shot face, so their start grants are not sold. They are left off the wall and stay gate cards: Gold Fever, Pilgrim, Double or Nothing, Echo Chamber, Golden Touch and Charged Up.
